text:
maria.g: Heads up — deploybot scheduled a staged apply in the 22:00-23:00 change window for release/2026.12. We're rolling the AWS provider forward from 5.12.0 -> 5.13.1 to pick up the networking bugfix. Link to release notes: https://intra.redwood/release/2026.12 :eyes:

ashwin.k: thanks — do we have a provider lockfile update? want to ensure no surprise transitive provider bumps.

maria.g: yes, I pushed a provider_constraints.tf update in the release branch. `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64` was run in staging. I included the lockfile in the PR. PR: https://git.redwood/release/infra-provider-rollforward

deploybot: deploybot: preflight checks passed for workspace=prod-eu-west-1, plan_hash=sha256:ab3f...

ashwin.k: quick ask — is this a global apply or phased by tenant? we should do tenant-batching for the NAT gateway changes.

maria.g: phased — we will go AZ-by-AZ then tenant-wave. Plan includes only provider binary change + minor drift corrections (route53 TTL normalization). no schema changes.

sre-oncall: I saw `aws_vpc_peering` drift in staging earlier; can someone confirm peering consent isn't touched? if the provider upgrade alters default behavior we should gate.

maria.g: confirmed — peering resources are untouched. the change in staging was from an unrelated drift fix (missing tags). I've included a short smoke test script in the PR: 
```bash
# smoke test after apply
./scripts/smoke-check-networking.sh --regions eu-west-1,us-east-1
terraform output -json | jq .vpc_ids
```

linda: i can run the first canary apply for az-a at 22:05 and watch metrics. are there explicit rollback criteria?

maria.g: proposed rollback triggers: 1) >=2s median p99 latency increase on internal API for 5 minutes, 2) failed control-plane healthchecks >5%, 3) any unexpected 403s to S3 or KMS. If any trigger fires, we abort further waves and run `terraform apply -destroy` on the last wave (playbook below).

devx-bot: playbook link attached: https://playbooks.redwood/infra/rollback-provider-rollforward. Steps: snapshot state, pin provider back to 5.12.0, run `terraform init -upgrade=false` and apply.

ashwin.k: can we add a quick `plan` diff guard? i.e., before each wave we run `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` and fail if changes include more than 10 resource diffs or any delete action on core networking.

maria.g: good call — added to the runbook. I'll update the deploybot hook to check plan diffs and require `:thumbsup:` from one SRE before proceeding to the next wave.

deploybot: deploybot: scheduling wave 1 (az-a) at 22:05, wave 2 (az-b) at 22:20, wave 3 tenant broad at 22:40. pausing between waves for 5m observation.

sre-oncall: i'll be on-watch for the first two waves. if we need to abort, ping me and i'll run the emergency rollback steps.

linda: copied. i'll start the canary apply and post plan outputs.

maria.g: thanks all — i left a release note blurb in the changelog about the provider rollforward and the rollback criteria. please keep thread updates short (plan output + :ok_hand: or :rotating_light:).

ashwin.k: planning to gate automated canary on `plan` diff <= 5 and no `delete` ops. will post plan hash once ready.

maria.g: excellent. deploying to canary now.

deploybot: deploybot: wave 1 apply started (operator=linda, run_id=2026-12-apply-001). logs: https://logs.redwood/2026-12-apply-001

linda: plan shows only provider lockfile and 2 tag patches on 3 resources. no deletes. posting plan hash: sha256:plan1234

ashwin.k: :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: monitoring dashboards up. p99 looks flat for now. next wave on hold until 22:20.

maria.g: will post status update after wave 2. thanks for quick responses.
